answer: A proof-of-burn protocol forces agents to permanently destroy native tokens to record their operational key in the network atlas. Because verifiers mandate on-chain burn proofs, an attacker cannot forge synthetic peers without incurring the unrecoverable cost of sacrificed liquid capital per identity. This dynamic creates a robust economic oasis against mass replication. A key limitation is that non-refundable entry costs unfairly penalize capital-constrained honest agents.
